newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs close mostly off after Dec sets new high.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs close mostly off after Dec sets new high.

text.p: Early demand that saw December CME hog futures run up to a new contract high dissipated late and most months slipped for losses by the close on profit taking and local selling, traders said.
Hog futures closed 0.125 cent higher to 0.325 lower with February off 0.300 at 75.450 cents. December posted a new contract high early of 60.475 before ending at 60.125 cents.

December continued to be supported by weather-reduced hog runs and light deliveries. Bitter cold weather over much of the midsection of the country has made it hard to sort and morket hogs, adding to tight deliveries, they said.
"Deliveries have been too light to press the market. There's hogs out there, but not the ones that can be delivered," one trader said.
However, after the close the CME posted 25 deliveries against the December contract for Wednesday which may weigh on December futures Wednesday morning.
"If cash is not higher, then futures may open lower" based on the deliveries, said Dennis Smith, broker with LIT division of First Options.

Deferred contracts slipped on profit-taking and local selling with sell stops touched off under early lows, basis February. That month and April had been supported early by projections on the upcoming Hogs and Pigs report. The report is expected to show increased retention of breeding stock which will tighten marketings in the near term and result in increased hog numbers later, traders added.

Early estimates on the report point to all hogs on farms at 99 to 100 percent of last year with numbers kept for breeding at 100 to 103 percent and hogs kept for market at 98 to 99 percent of last year.
In hog options, First Chicago bought October 60 and 62 calls and February 78 and 80 calls. ASK, division of Shatkin, bought April 70 puts, pit sources added.
Pork bellies fell to new day's lows late before local short covering pared losses by the close and prices ended 0.325 to 0.575 cent lower with February off 0.325 at 77.375 cents.
Light hog kills are supportive, but weakness in cash weighed on prices, they said.
After the close, the CME reported a net in-movement of 1.774 million lbs of bellies into out-of-town warehouses, in the range of early estimates of in 1.0 to 2.5 million lbs.
